wholeQuestion.question: A new screening tool has very high sensitivity but low specificity. What is the most likely operational consequence?
choices: More false positive referrals for assessment
wholeQuestion.rationale: High sensitivity captures most at risk patients, while low specificity increases false positives.

choiceReview.choice: More false positive referrals for assessment
choiceReview.assessment: Low specificity entails more false positives among those without the target condition, increasing assessment referrals.
High sensitivity does not imply more false negatives.
A positive screen does not remove the need for assessment.
High sensitivity with low specificity is not perfect accuracy.

wholeQuestion.question: Why is interrater reliability important for a nutrition focused physical examination?
choices: Different clinicians should classify the same findings consistently
It proves the findings cause mortality
wholeQuestion.rationale: Reliability addresses consistency, not causal validity.

questions.sourceLocation: COSMIN2010 native pages4/9; reliability is distinct from validity

choiceReview.choice: Different clinicians should classify the same findings consistently
choiceReview.assessment: Interrater reliability concerns consistency between clinicians.

choiceReview.choice: It proves the findings cause mortality
choiceReview.assessment: Agreement between raters does not establish a causal mortality relationship.
Rater agreement does not replace comparison with a criterion.
Reliability does not eliminate all measurement error.

wholeQuestion.question: What is spectrum bias in validation of a malnutrition screen?
choices: Performance changes because the study population does not represent the intended clinical spectrum
The tool contains too many colors
The same assessor repeats a measurement
wholeQuestion.rationale: A tool validated only in a narrow severity range may perform differently in broader practice.

questions.sourceLocation: STARD2016 native pages1/11, items20/21 population and disease spectrum

choiceReview.choice: Performance changes because the study population does not represent the intended clinical spectrum
choiceReview.assessment: Accuracy may vary with severity and alternative-diagnosis mix; a narrow population may not represent the intended population.

choiceReview.choice: The tool contains too many colors
choiceReview.assessment: Color count is not the clinical spectrum.

choiceReview.choice: The same assessor repeats a measurement
choiceReview.assessment: Repeated measurement by one assessor is not spectrum bias.
Blinding the reference assessor is a different methodological issue.

wholeQuestion.question: Why should a clinical decision threshold be prespecified before validating a screening score?
choices: Post hoc threshold selection can exaggerate apparent performance
wholeQuestion.rationale: Selecting the best threshold after seeing results can overfit the sample.

questions.sourceLocation: STARD2016 native page7, item12 prespecified versus exploratory cutoffs

choiceReview.choice: Post hoc threshold selection can exaggerate apparent performance
choiceReview.assessment: Selecting a cutoff that maximizes observed performance can yield optimistic accuracy in that sample.
Sensitivity remains relevant after a threshold is chosen.
A fixed threshold does not guarantee performance in a different population.
Prespecification does not remove missing observations.

wholeQuestion.question: What is the best method to test whether a translated screening tool retains construct validity?
choices: Evaluate measurement structure and associations in the target language population
Translate each word literally and assume equivalence
wholeQuestion.rationale: Translation requires cultural and psychometric validation in the target population.

questions.sourceLocation: COSMIN2010 native pages4/9/10, construct and cross-cultural validity

choiceReview.choice: Evaluate measurement structure and associations in the target language population
choiceReview.assessment: Assess the construct structure and expected associations in the target-language population; do not assume linguistic equivalence.

choiceReview.choice: Translate each word literally and assume equivalence
choiceReview.assessment: Literal word translation alone does not establish measurement validity.
Font comparison does not test the construct.
The original-language sample cannot establish performance of the translated version in the target population.

COSMIN2010.scopeLimit: COSMIN paper focuses on health-related patient-reported instruments. Used here for general distinctions between reliability, validity, construct structure and target-language measurement; no nutrition-screen-specific validation or endorsement inferred.
